title: Geodesic Quantum $f$-Divergences
abstract: We introduce the geodesic quantum $f$-divergences $D_f^t$, $0\leq t\leq1$, obtained from the affine-invariant geodesic between the standard and maximal relative modular operators. They reduce to the classical $f$-divergence for commuting states. The logarithmic generator yields geodesic relative entropies joining the Umegaki and Belavkin-Staszewski entropies, while the power generators yield $(t,α)$-Rényi divergences joining the Petz and geometric families.   Our first main result is data processing of $D_f^t$ for every finite operator-convex generator $f$ and every $t\in[0,1]$. In particular, this gives DPI for the geodesic relative entropies and for the $(t,α)$-Rényi divergences when $0<α<1$ or $1<α\leq2$. Our second main result identifies equality in the DPI: for invertible states, every equality-determining operator-convex generator has, at each nonmaximal parameter $0\leq t<1$, exactly the Petz sufficiency class; at $t=1$, this changes to the generally larger maximal, or BS, class, which also coincides with the equality class of the divergences associated with the quadratic generator for every $t$. Our third main result is the corresponding collapse of invertible geodesic quantum Markov chains: for each of the three ordered conditional-mutual-information constructions, the $t$-quantum Markov chains are precisely the quantum Markov chains for $0\leq t<1$, whereas at $t=1$ they are the invertible BS quantum Markov chains, a class that can be strictly larger.   We also determine parameter-monotonicity regimes and the intersections with the $(α,z)$ family. We prove strengthened data-processing and reconstruction estimates; we compare the three conditional orientations; we establish continuity bounds under positive lower-eigenvalue assumptions together with complementary discontinuity results; and we give a capacity-per-unit-cost interpretation.
summary: The paper develops the concept of geodesic quantum f-divergences by interpolating between standard and maximal relative modular operators. It proves key properties like data processing inequalities (DPI) across this entire family of divergences. This work unifies several important measures in quantum information theory, providing deep insights into how information quantities behave under physical operations.
main_problem: The paper introduces and analyzes geodesic quantum f-divergences, $D_f^t$, which generalize classical f-divergences to the noncommuting setting of quantum states.
main_result: It establishes data processing inequalities (DPI) for these divergences and characterizes the equality conditions, showing a transition in the required sufficiency class at the parameter $t=1$.
method: The analysis uses the affine-invariant geodesic approach between standard and maximal relative modular operators to construct the divergence family.
model_or_system: The framework applies to quantum states ($ho$, $\sigma$) and involves interpolating between known quantum divergences like Umegaki, Belavkin-Staszewski (BS), Petz, and Rényi entropies.
key_observables: Geodesic quantum $f$-divergences ($D_t^f$), relative entropies, conditional mutual information, and various generalized entropy measures.
important_parameters: The interpolation parameter $t \in [0, 1]$ controls the specific divergence used; the generator function $f$ determines the family type.
main_assumptions: Results are primarily derived for invertible quantum states, though extensions to non-invertible cases are discussed. The analysis relies on assuming operator-convex generators $f$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 is mentioned as illustrating how different divergences interpolate between endpoints (Petz and geometric Rényi).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the geodesic divergence, proving its data processing properties for all $t$, identifying the conditions for equality in DPI, and finally analyzing the collapse of quantum Markov chains at different values of $t$.
why_interesting: This work provides a unified mathematical structure (the geodesic) to study how various fundamental measures of distinguishability and information flow behave as they interpolate between known limits, which is crucial for understanding physical processes in open quantum systems.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Specialization diagram for the (t, f)-divergences. Teal arrows select a generator (with the Rényi normalization included on the upper branch), while dark blue and orange arrows select the Petz endpoint t = 0 and the maximal endpoint t = 1, respectively. The dotted vertical arrows show that the two operations commute. Thus Dt interpolates between the Umegaki and BS relative entropies, and Dt α interpolates between the Petz and geometric Rényi divergences. At α = 2 the entire upper row coincides even for noncommuting states; for commuting states every horizontal row collapses to its common classical quantity.

Figure 2: Rényi interpolation for the states in (74). The dark blue and orange boundary curves are, respectively, the Petz-Rényi divergences D0 α = Dα and the geometric Rényi divergence D1 α = bDα. The contrasting teal curves show Dt α for t = k/20, k = 1, . . . , 19, and the light teal band represents the full continuum 0 ≤t ≤1. The values at α = 0 and α = 1 are the continuous extensions Dt 0 = 0 and Dt 1 = Dt. The marked order-one points are the relative and BS entropies, and the order-two marker is their common Rényi value .

Figure 3: Comparison of the (t, α) and (α, z) Rényi families for the same noncommuting states as in Figure 2. Teal denotes the complete t-interpolation band and violet the compactified DPI-admissible (α, z) value band in (107); thin curves sample their interiors. The navy, orange, and solid-violet boundaries are, respectively, the shared Petz, geometric, and sandwiched divergences. The labels mark the order-one Umegaki and BS limits and the order-two Petz and sandwiched points. Any overlap of the shaded bands is specific to this fixed pair.
